title: Graph Sharp-Threshold Approximation by Monotone DNF
statement: There is a function $w:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb N$ with the following property. For all $v,n\in\mathbb N$, every bijection from the $n$ coordinates to the two-element subsets of a labeled $v$-vertex set, and every increasing Boolean graph property $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ invariant under permutations of the vertices, let $p,K,\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<p\le\tfrac12$, $K>0$, and $0<\varepsilon<1$. If the biased total influence of $f$ at parameter $p$ is at most $K$, then there is a monotone DNF formula $d$ of width at most $w(K,\varepsilon)$ whose probability of disagreement with $f$ under the Bernoulli-$p$ product weights is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: A bijection from the $n$ coordinates to the two-element subsets of the labeled $v$-vertex set
$f$ is invariant under every vertex permutation acting on the edge coordinates
Biased total influence of $f$ at $p$ is at most $K$
replaced: There exists $w:\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb N$ such that whenever the $n$ variables bijectively index the edges of a labeled simple graph on $v$ vertices, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ is an increasing graph property, $0<p\le1/2$, $K>0$, $0<\varepsilon<1$, and $I_p(f)\le K$, there is a monotone DNF $d$ of width at most $w(K,\varepsilon)$ with $\Pr_p(f\ne d)\le\varepsilon$. Here $I_p(f)=4p(1-p)$ times the sum of pivotal probabilities.
